column3: Now, let’s learn about human reproduction!
You've learned about the many parts of the reproductive system in the previous chapter.
This is where you'll see their functions in action.
In girls, the ovaries release an egg cell into the fallopian tubes every month.
The egg cell then travels through the fallopian tubes.
During sexual intercourse, a man inserts his penis into a woman’s vagina.
When a man ejaculates during this, he releases semen, a fluid full of sperm cells.
If there are sperm present in the fallopian tubes, the sperm and egg cells unite and they turn into a zygote.
This zygote then goes to the uterus and eventually grows into a baby.
Usually, the baby is born after 9 months.
However, this does not always result in pregnancy, as only a small amount of sperm end up making it to the fallopian tubes.
Moreover, the chance for pregnancy is usually lower during a woman’s period, but it can still happen anyway! It’s just less likely.
